Why owning money once made people feel hunted.

Kevin Trudeau tells a story about a farmer on the prairie. A dying rider hands him a bag of gold and asks only for a burial.

The farmer doesn't feel safe. He feels hunted, because back then there were no banks, and anyone holding money became a target.

Kevin says that kind of fear can be passed down through families and sit quietly under what we believe about money today.

What did your family teach you about having money?

You thought it was a snake. It was only a rope.

Kevin Trudeau uses a dark basement to explain enlightenment. You bump into things and see a shadow coiled in the corner, and you are sure it's a snake.

Then someone turns on the light and you see it's just a rope.

For Kevin, enlightenment is seeing what is really there.

What fear in your life might turn out to be a rope?
